breaking.headline: S&P 500 sinks further as seventh straight loss deepens; VIX tops 32
breaking.fact: The S&P 500 was down about 2.2% near midday Friday, on track for a seventh straight loss and its worst week since April 2025, while the Nasdaq fell 3.6% and the VIX jumped above 32; the Dow held up better, off about 0.7%. Chip stocks sank again, with Nvidia down about 7%.

breaking.headline: Intuit plunges after cutting outlook and selling Mailchimp at a steep loss
breaking.fact: Intuit fell about 10% Friday after cutting its fiscal 2027 revenue outlook — slashing Credit Karma growth guidance to 3-7% as consumers turn to AI chatbots for financial products — and agreeing to sell Mailchimp to Bending Spoons for $3.68 billion, under a third of the roughly $12 billion it paid in 2021.

breaking.headline: Senate rejects Iran war-powers resolution, 51-48
breaking.fact: The Senate voted 51-48 Thursday to reject a House-passed resolution directing President Trump to end the war in Iran or seek Congress's approval, the first such vote since the midterm elections; only three Republicans backed it and one Democrat opposed it.

breaking.headline: BILL Holdings to go private in $6 billion TPG deal
breaking.fact: Private equity firm TPG agreed to take fintech BILL Holdings private in a $6 billion all-cash deal, part of roughly $91 billion in transactions in about 24 hours alongside Anthropic's record IPO and Intuit's Mailchimp sale.

weekInBrief.headline: Anthropic's record debut fades on day two
weekInBrief.body: Anthropic closed its first day of trading Thursday at $97.17, up 17% from its $83 IPO price, after opening at $111.50 — a debut that raised $81.3 billion, the largest IPO on record. By midday Friday the shares had given back much of it, down about 13% to near $84, as the AI selloff swept the market.

weekInBrief.headline: Dow closes below 50,000 for first time since June
weekInBrief.body: The Dow fell 1,101 points Thursday, or 2.19%, to 49,097.06, its first close below 50,000 since June, as the S&P 500 logged a sixth straight loss and the Nasdaq fell 2.25% on another broad selloff.

weekInBrief.headline: Bitcoin slides toward $61,000 as risk rout spreads
weekInBrief.body: Bitcoin traded near $61,500 Friday, down sharply on the week as the selloff spread from stocks to crypto; the slide came as investors dumped AI-linked shares, the dollar firmed, and gold fell to a 14-month low.

weekInBrief.headline: Texas regulators resume data-center permits before ordered review is done
weekInBrief.body: The Texas Commission on Environmental Quality has resumed approving data-center permits even though the community-impact review Gov. Greg Abbott ordered in September is not yet complete — a decision with direct implications for the state's power-grid buildout as data-center demand surges.

items.headline: Latest from the Strait
items.body: U.S. Central Command widened its blockade on Wednesday, warning that any vessel taking on Iranian-linked cargo in a ship-to-ship transfer automatically becomes a blockade-evasion target that can be stopped, boarded, diverted or captured — the move followed the transfer of about 200,000 barrels of Iranian crude Tuesday from the sanctioned Suezmax Olym to the tanker Hao Fan, the first such movement since July, according to Kpler and United Against Nuclear Iran. Iranian media floated sending a tanker convoy to China in defiance of the blockade, the New York Times reported new U.S. strikes are under consideration, and President Trump said he is in no hurry to decide on Iran before January 1. On oil, the roughly 200,000 barrels transferred Tuesday has not left the Gulf as an export, while about 8.3 million barrels a day of non-Iranian oil and products kept flowing through the strait in the week to November 11, about 48% of pre-war levels.

space.headline: Starship Flight 17 hardware in cryo testing as SpaceX eyes first Florida launch
space.body: SpaceX's Flight 17 hardware — Ship 44 and Booster 24 — is in cryo testing at Starbase, with the mission set to carry a larger load of production Starlink V3 satellites. SpaceX hopes to fly Starship from Kennedy Space Center's Pad 39A by the end of 2026, attempting a booster catch at the Florida tower before the Ship returns to Texas after about eight or nine hours in orbit.

space.headline: NASA's Fermi telescope finds a pulsar a million times faster
space.body: An international team found a new pulsar, PSR J1622-7204, spinning 261 times a second in public data from NASA's Fermi Gamma-ray Space Telescope, using a cryptography-inspired search method about a million times faster than previous searches. The paper appeared Nov. 19 in Physical Review Letters, and researchers hope to pair the method with volunteer computing to find more pulsars.

space.headline: Astronomers watch two stars merge in the Andromeda galaxy
space.body: Astronomers have reconstructed a rare stellar merger in the Andromeda galaxy, an unusually detailed view of two stars becoming one. Published Nov. 18 in Nature, the findings offer important evidence for common-envelope evolution, a poorly understood stage of binary-star development.

space.headline: How the brain uses the past to shape what we perceive
space.body: Neuroscientists at Italy's International School for Advanced Studies have identified a neural mechanism explaining why identical sensations can feel different depending on what happened moments earlier. Published Nov. 19 in Science Advances, the findings point to specialized inhibitory neurons that weave immediate sensations together with short-term experience.

apod.credit: NASA/Anil Menon — NASA Image of the Day, November 17, 2026
